Open the App Store to review and install them.
Android only lets the store update apps it installed, so these need your tap. Open the App Store to install them.
Tells you when apps you installed here have a newer version.
When on, updates install when found. When off, they wait for a tap. Store-installed apps update silently; the rest just notify.

Tap to see how this source is checked
Apps built for anything older than API %1$d are not listed, and are turned away at install even if the listing said otherwise. Old apps skip the sandbox and permission rules newer Android enforces.
Every download has its signature checked. A file with no valid signature never gets installed.
The app has to be the one you asked for
The name inside the downloaded file must match the app you tapped install on.
An update has to be signed by the same key as the copy you already have, or a key that one was rotated to. Anything else is refused.
Some apps arrive as several files. All of them must be signed by the same key, so a swapped part cannot slip in with the real ones.
Everything is checked before the download reaches the system installer. Rejected files are deleted.
A failed check blocks, a missing one warns
If a check fails, the install stops. If a source publishes nothing to check against, the app installs but is marked unverified.
Nothing else on your phone can quietly replace an app you installed here.
The sources below are built in and you cannot add more. Nothing above could be promised for a repo you added yourself.

The sources here protect you in different ways, and none of them is simply the safest. Each card says what the source does itself, what this app checks on the download, and where that source is weaker than the others.
These hold wherever the app came from. Each source adds its own on top.
Modern Apps downloads have to be signed by this key. It is read off your phone at install time, so it is always the key this copy of the store was really signed with.
Couldn\'t read this app\'s signing key.
There is no way to pull a bad release off phones that already took it.
Built in the same repo as this store and signed with the same key, which your phone can check against the copy of the store you are holding.
All of it is open source, in one public repository
Every app ships from one tagged release, signed with one key
The repository index is signed and checked against this store\'s own pinned key
Signed by this app\'s own key, read straight from your phone at install time
The file matches the hash in the repository\'s signed index
One developer, one key, no independent review and nobody rebuilding the source to confirm the app matches it. There is no scanning.
Built from public source code. Versions a second machine independently rebuilt to an identical file are badged as reproducible.
Every app is built from source F-Droid publishes, not from a binary a developer sent in
A second build server rebuilds many apps and compares the result byte for byte
Tracking, ads and non-free dependencies are labelled on the listing
F-Droid\'s app list is signed, and checked against a key built into this store
Every entry in that list is chained back to the signature
Versions F-Droid\'s second build server reproduced bit-for-bit are badged as reproducible
The hash and the signing key both come from the signed list

F-Droid holds the signing key, not the developer, so its build servers can sign anything. Nobody checks what an app does, only that it matches its source. Updates wait to be rebuilt, which can take days or weeks, security fixes included.
Developer-built apps, listed only when an independent builder reproduced the exact version bit-for-bit from published source.
Apps are the developers\' own signed builds, taken from their release pages
Independent verification builders rebuild each covered version from its published source tag and compare the result byte for byte
Listings are screened and badged with the result, visible in this store as a reproducible badge
IzzyOnDroid\'s app list is signed, and checked against a key built into this store
Every entry in that list is chained back to the signature
Only versions an independent builder reproduced bit-for-bit are listed at all
The hash and the signing key both come from the signed list

The signing key belongs to the developer, so a reproduced build still trusts that developer\'s release pipeline — the rebuild only proves the binary matches the published source. Versions no builder has covered are not offered here. Nobody scans what an app does.
Reviewed, scanned and signed by Google, who verify who the developer is and can pull an app from every phone at once.
Developers have to prove who they are, with a real name and address on file
Every upload is scanned, and Play Protect keeps scanning apps on the phone afterwards
Signing keys are held in hardware security modules rather than on a build server
A malicious app can be removed from the store and disabled on phones within hours
Each downloaded file matches the hash Google sent with it
Signed by the key Google lists for this app
The app\'s publisher stamp is saved the first time you install it, and has to stay the same afterwards

No source code and no second build, so nothing proves the app matches any source. Google supplies both the file and the expectation, catching a tampered download but not a bad update Google signs itself. This store\'s anonymous account sees less than the Play app.
Apps signed by their own developers, listed on Accrescent\'s ed25519-signed allowlist which pins each app\'s signing key and lowest allowed version.
Each app is signed by its developer\'s own key, not by Accrescent
Which apps are legitimate, and each one\'s expected key, come from a single ed25519-signed list
The list records a minimum version per app, so an old build can\'t be pushed back onto you
The app list is signed and checked against a key built into this store, with a timestamp that can never go backwards
The download is signed by exactly the key the signed list names for this app
The download\'s version is at or above the minimum the signed list allows

Accrescent publishes no per-file hashes and no reproducible builds, so the guarantee is the signature and minimum version, not source. Listings come from an ordinary server over gRPC; a bad response can only produce a file that fails these checks. Nobody scans the apps.
Curated free-but-proprietary apps fetched from Google Play by this store\'s own server and published in a signed index naming each version\'s hash and signing key.
Only an explicit allowlist is mirrored, chosen by the store operator
Versions, file hashes and expected signing keys are published in an index signed with this store\'s release key
The files are the developers\' own Play builds, fetched unchanged rather than rebuilt
That signed index is checked against a key built into this store
Every downloaded file matches the hash and the signing key that index names for it
These are closed-source apps fetched by the operator, so you trust the operator to have fetched the genuine file, and there is no source to audit and no reproducible build. Nobody scans the apps.
